subject: storytime
title: The Three Billy Goats Gruff
about: The Norwegian folk tale of three goats who must cross a grumpy troll's bridge to reach the green grass on the hill; in this telling the big goat butts the troll into the river, and he simply floats away. Three crossings with the same trip, trap and the same questions make it easy to read with expression and to retell in order. It is a public-domain story retold here in first-grade words, five pages long.
tip: Read the goats in three voices, tiny, middle and big, and stamp out every trip, trap with your feet.

book.author: a folk tale from Norway (retold)
book.source: public domain, retold in first-grade words
book.blurb: Three goats, one bridge, and one very grumpy troll.

passage.text:
Once there were three billy goats named Gruff.
One was little.
One was middle-sized.
One was big.
They wanted the green grass on the hill.
To get there, they had to cross a bridge.
And under the bridge lived a grumpy troll.
***
The little goat went first.
Trip, trap! Trip, trap!
"Who is that on my bridge?" roared the troll.
"It is me, the little goat."
"I will gobble you up!" said the troll.
"Please do not eat me," said the little goat.
"Wait for my brother."
"He is much bigger."
"Then go," said the troll.
And over he went.
***
Next the middle goat went.
Trip, trap! Trip, trap!
"Who is that on my bridge?" roared the troll.
"It is me, the middle goat."
"I will gobble you up!" said the troll.
"Please do not eat me," said the middle goat.
"Wait for my big brother."
"He is much, much bigger."
"Then go," said the troll.
And over he went.
***
Then the big goat went.
Trip, trap! Trip, trap!
The bridge shook.
"Who is that on my bridge?" roared the troll.
"It is me, the big goat!"
"I will gobble you up!" said the troll.
"Come and try!" said the big goat.
Up jumped the troll.
The big goat put down his horns.
Bump!
He butted the troll off the bridge.
***
Splash!
The troll fell into the river.
He floated far, far away.
The big goat trip-trapped over the bridge.
All three goats went up the hill.
They ate and ate the sweet green grass.
Munch, munch, munch!
And the grumpy troll never came back.

cards.q: Who said, 'Who is that on my bridge?'
cards.note: The troll asks the same thing three times, so read it in a big, grumpy voice.

cards.q: What did the goats want to eat?
cards.note: The best grass was on the hill, and the only way there was over the troll's bridge.

cards.q: What did the little goat tell the troll to do?
cards.note: The two smaller goats each send the troll on to a bigger brother, which is a clever way to get across.
Splash: in this telling he just floats far away and never comes back.

cards.q: What happened first in the story?
cards.note: Little, then middle, then big: the goats cross from smallest to biggest.

cards.q: What happened at the end of the story?
cards.note: All three goats got to the hill at last and ate the sweet green grass.
The story calls him grumpy, and he roars every time a goat steps on his bridge.
Most of the story happens on that bridge, so ask him to draw it with the troll underneath.

cards.q: In the story, what does 'butted' mean?
cards.note: Goats butt with their heads and horns; press your forehead gently on his hand to show him.

cards.q: Which word is in the story?
cards.note: He reads the three words himself; only one of them is in the story.
